currency_note: Zijin reports in RMB (CAS/China Accounting Standards; CNY is the functional and presentation currency for both the A-share 601899.SH and H-share 2899.HK filings), while the H-share quote on HKEX is denominated in HKD. There is no separate HKD-denominated financial statement -- the H-share price is simply a CNY-earnings stock quoted in a different trading currency. Any DCF or multiples work on 2899.HK must bridge CNY financials to an HKD (or USD) valuation via an explicit fx_rate; dividing the HKD quote directly by CNY per-share metrics without that bridge will produce a materially wrong multiple (same class of error documented on other RMB/HKD dual-currency H-shares).
overview: Zijin Mining is a Chinese multinational mining group, dual-listed with A-shares on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (601899) and H-shares on HKEX (2899), engaged in the exploration, development, mining and processing of gold, copper, zinc, lithium, silver, molybdenum and other metals. The Group operates more than 30 large-scale mineral resource bases across 17 overseas countries (including the DRC, Serbia, Papua New Guinea, Peru, Kazakhstan, Argentina, Tajikistan, Ghana, Guyana, Suriname, Colombia and Australia) plus 17 Chinese provinces/regions, and in 2025 became the world's third-largest mining company by market capitalization (behind only BHP and Rio Tinto), and the world's largest gold-mining enterprise by most metrics.

business_model.summary: Zijin makes money primarily from mining and selling gold and copper (concentrate, cathode/electrolytic and electrodeposited metal), supplemented by zinc, silver, lithium carbonate and by-product molybdenum/tungsten/sulphuric acid/iron. Revenue is transactional/commodity-price-linked (sold at prevailing market metal prices, not contracted/recurring), heavily geared to gold and copper prices, and the mix spans wholly-owned, majority-owned and minority/associate-owned mines consolidated on an attributable basis. Zijin is vertically integrated from ore extraction through smelting/refining for its core copper and gold assets, which supports low unit costs. FY2025 operating income was RMB349.1bn (+15% YoY) with net profit attributable to owners of RMB51.8bn (+62% YoY); H1 2026 operating income was RMB194.2bn (+15.8% YoY) with net profit attributable to owners after non-recurring items of RMB38.0bn (+76% YoY), driven by a historic gold/silver price surge and record copper prices.

revenue_streams.name: Gold (mined + refined/trading)
revenue_streams.note: H1 2026: 41.2% of operating income after elimination, 41.7% of gross profit; benefiting disproportionately from the 2025-26 gold price spike

revenue_streams.name: Copper (concentrate, cathode, electrodeposited)
revenue_streams.note: H1 2026: 32.6% of operating income, 33.8% of gross profit; FY2025 full-year copper was 27.6% of income / 34.5% of gross profit

revenue_streams.name: Silver
revenue_streams.note: Silver prices roughly tripled YoY in H1 2026

revenue_streams.name: Lithium (carbonate/salts, concentrate)
revenue_streams.note: Explicitly framed by management as the company's 'third growth driver'; H1 2026 LCE output +496% YoY off a small base

revenue_streams.name: Other (molybdenum, tungsten, iron, cobalt, sulphuric acid/sulphur)
revenue_streams.note: Increasingly material profit contributor via comprehensive by-product utilisation

business_model.customer_type: B2B -- sells concentrate, refined metal and by-products to smelters, traders, fabricators and (for gold) the bullion market; no direct consumer exposure
business_model.geographic_mix: Mine assets split roughly between China (legacy base: Fujian, Tibet/Julong, Heilongjiang, Jilin, Shanxi, Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, Anhui) and overseas (DRC copper/cobalt/lithium, Serbia copper/gold, Kazakhstan/Tajikistan/Kyrgyzstan gold, Ghana/Guyana/Suriname/Colombia/Australia/PNG gold, Peru/Argentina copper-gold-lithium); overseas assets now supply a large and rising share of incremental copper, gold and lithium growth.

main_competitors: Chifeng Gold (now a controlled Zijin subsidiary)
competitive_position.market_position: Top-3 global mining company by market capitalization (~US$100bn+, behind BHP and Rio Tinto, ahead of Glencore as of late 2025); world's No.1 gold producer by most measures and ranked among the top 3-4 global copper producers; the only Asian/Chinese miner producing over 1 million tonnes of mined copper annually for three consecutive years; ranked 181st on the 2026 Forbes Global 2000 (up 70 places YoY) and 325th on the Fortune Global 500.

moat_factors.description: Retained resources of >4,600 tonnes gold, ~110 million tonnes copper, >12 million tonnes zinc/lead, and >18 million tonnes lithium carbonate equivalent as of end-2025 -- one of the largest diversified base-and-precious-metal resource inventories outside the majors

Company explicitly anchors strategy on 'low-cost mine operations' and cost leadership via technology, electrification/automation and whole-process in-house engineering; historically among the lowest-cost gold and copper producers globally

Aggressive, successful dual-driver strategy of acquisition plus organic exploration (Kamoa-Kakula, Julong, Serbia Zijin Copper, Rosebel, Akyem, Raygorodok, Zangge Mining, Chifeng Gold, Gansu Northwest Gold, Lianrui Mining/tungsten-tin) consistently adding resources below replacement cost ahead of peers
Repeated pattern of bringing major growth projects (Julong phase 2, Manono lithium, Lakkor Tso, Raygorodok/Akyem upgrades) into production ahead of schedule

Minxi Xinghang State-owned Assets Investment Company (controlled by Shanghang County, Fujian) is the largest shareholder (~24-26% historically), giving Zijin preferential standing with Chinese regulators/financing and alignment with China's critical-minerals security strategy, though it is not a central SOE
Gold-copper-lithium 'three pillar' strategy plus molybdenum/tungsten/zinc/silver by-products reduces single-commodity and single-country risk versus narrower peers

weaknesses: Heavy and growing reliance on politically unstable or higher-risk jurisdictions (DRC, Serbia, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, PNG) for growth capacity
Minority/JV structure at key growth assets (Kamoa-Kakula ~44.2% attributable, Julong 58%, Yulong only 22%) means headline production figures overstate Zijin's attributable economic exposure
Complex, sprawling corporate structure (Zijin Gold International and Zangge Mining now separately listed, Chifeng Gold being consolidated) increases governance and minority-interest complexity
Chinese SOE-adjacent ownership and A+H dual listing create perceived geopolitical/ESG overhang for some Western institutional investors
History of environmental/community friction at overseas assets (Serbia Bor pollution protests, periodic production suspensions)

growth_drivers: Kamoa-Kakula copper expansion (DRC) -- long-run growth project even though 2026 output was cut (290-330kt company-wide 2026 plan vs 380-420kt pre-flood) following the 2025 seismic event/flooding; dewatering and ramp-up ongoing

Julong Copper Mine (Tibet) phase 2 upgrade completed and in production, targeting 300-350kt/yr, with phase 3 approval potentially lifting output toward ~600kt/yr, positioning Julong as the world's largest-scale, highest-altitude, lowest-grade super-large copper mine

Lithium build-out ('third growth driver'): Lakkor Tso Salar (Tibet), Tres Quebradas Salar (Argentina), Xiangyuan Hard Rock Lithium Mine, Manono Lithium Mine (DRC) and Zangge Mining -- guidance of 270,000-320,000 tonnes LCE by 2028 from a near-zero 2024 base

Gold growth via Zijin Gold International platform (Akyem, Raygorodok, Rosebel technological upgrades) plus the pending consolidation of Chifeng Gold (~RMB18.3bn / ~US$2.6bn deal for effective control, closing H2 2026) adding six gold mines across China, Southeast Asia and West Africa
Serbia copper-gold complex (Čukaru Peki + Bor) expansion toward 450kt/yr combined copper capacity, which would make it Europe's largest copper producer
Molybdenum scale-up via the Shapinggou Molybdenum Mine (world's largest standalone molybdenum reserve) targeting 25,000-35,000 tonnes/yr by 2028

Continued bolt-on M&A (Gansu Northwest Gold, Lianrui Mining/tungsten-tin, prior Allied Gold stake) funded by strong free cash flow and capital markets access (including a novel zero-coupon USD1.5bn H-share convertible bond)

Secular tailwinds: AI/data-center electrification and grid build-out driving structural copper demand ('computing power metal'); sovereign debt concerns, central bank reserve diversification and geopolitical risk driving a multi-year gold bull market; EV/storage demand supporting lithium recovery
Rising dividend payout ratio (raised from 30% to 35% of three-year cumulative distributable profit for 2026-2028) and accelerated interim dividend cadence

business.description: Revenue and margins are directly exposed to gold, copper, zinc, silver and lithium price swings; H1 2026 results were flattered by historic gold (+53% avg price YoY) and silver (+139%) and copper (+38%) price gains that may not repeat
2025 seismic event and flooding cut Kamoa-Kakula's 2026 output plan roughly in half (to 290-330kt from 380-420kt), directly pressuring Zijin's attributable 2026 copper production target
Large single mines (Julong, Kamoa-Kakula, Serbia complex) represent outsized shares of attributable copper and gold output; disruption at any one materially affects group production

Fast pace of acquisitions (Zangge Mining, Chifeng Gold, Gansu Northwest Gold, Lianrui Mining) and corporate restructuring (Zijin Gold International and Zangge Mining spin-off listings) raises execution and governance complexity

financial.description: Total assets grew from RMB208.6bn (2021) to RMB512.0bn (2025) and total liabilities from RMB115.7bn to RMB264.0bn over the same period, funding aggressive capex and M&A; debt-to-asset ratio was 49.55% at H1 2026 (first time below 50% since 2012), an improving but still elevated level for a capital-intensive miner

RMB-denominated financials with material USD, EUR, HKD, and other emerging-market currency (DRC franc, Serbian dinar, Kazakh tenge, PNG kina, etc.) revenue and cost exposures from its 18-country operating footprint; H-share HKD quote vs RMB financials also requires an explicit fx bridge for any cross-currency valuation work

Simultaneous major builds (Julong phase 3, Zhunuo, Manono, Lakkor Tso phase 2, Shapinggou, Serbia expansion, Haiyu) require sustained heavy capital expenditure, pressuring free cash flow even amid strong operating cash generation

regulatory.description: Management itself flags that 'resource-rich countries [are] strengthening their resource sovereignty' and that critical minerals are shifting from economic to strategic considerations; the Republic of Congo's 2026 ban on copper/cobalt concentrate exports illustrates the live risk across DRC-adjacent jurisdictions

History of Serbian regulatory fines and forced production halts at the Bor copper complex over air/water pollution and blasting; ongoing community protests represent recurring operational and reputational risk

Largest shareholder is a Fujian county-government-controlled state investment vehicle; this, combined with Chinese listing and some Western government scrutiny of Chinese mining investment in critical minerals and in jurisdictions like DRC, could affect market access, partnerships or financing in some markets

Large deals (Chifeng Gold, prior Allied Gold approach which was ultimately terminated) are subject to regulatory and shareholder approval processes that can fail or be delayed, as seen with the terminated Allied Gold acquisition in 2026

macro.description: Management explicitly cites exchange-rate and interest-rate volatility among major economies as repeatedly affecting metal prices; gold in particular is sensitive to real rates and USD strength

Management cited the Middle East conflict escalation as a driver of higher energy costs impacting unit costs in 2026; broader geopolitical fragmentation affects supply chains across the company's 18-country footprint

A meaningful share of smelting/processing and some mine assets remain domestic; a sharper China slowdown could pressure certain by-product and domestic demand-linked revenue lines, though global commodity pricing dominates overall results

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Structurally positive for Zijin's core commodities: gold supported by sovereign debt concerns, central bank reserve diversification and geopolitical risk (spot gold swung from ~USD5,500/oz highs to below USD4,000/oz in H1 2026, reflecting extreme volatility but a still-elevated price regime); copper supported by AI/data-center electrification, grid buildout and persistent supply-side underinvestment, with prices at or near record highs (>USD13,000-14,000/tonne) despite tariff-driven inventory distortions; lithium fundamentals improving on power-storage demand after a multi-year downturn, though volatile; zinc and strategic minor metals (molybdenum, tungsten) also firm on supply constraints and 'strategic demand'.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High -- Zijin is a leveraged play on global metal price cycles; earnings swung from RMB19.6bn net profit (2021) to RMB63.8bn (2025), more than tripling largely on commodity price appreciation rather than volume growth alone
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high indirectly: gold prices (a large share of group profit) are historically inversely correlated with real interest rates and USD strength; the company's own capex financing costs are also rate-sensitive given its scale of ongoing project investment
key_input_costs: Energy (diesel, electricity -- cited as a 2026 cost pressure from Middle East-driven energy price increases)

recent_developments.event: Analyst coverage remains uniformly bullish: Goldman Sachs reiterates Buy with HK$51 target (trimmed from HK$52 on higher energy-cost assumptions from Middle East tensions), still forecasting 2026 recurring profit of ~RMB77.9bn (+53% YoY); Jefferies Buy with HK$49.1 target assuming 2026 gold ~US$5,000/oz and copper ~US$5.7/lb; consensus on the A-shares shows 16 Buy ratings, no Hold/Sell

H1 2026 results released: net profit attributable to owners of RMB39.2bn (+68% YoY), after-non-recurring profit of RMB38.0bn (+76% YoY); management disclosed the Kamoa-Kakula flood could cut Zijin's attributable 2026 copper output by up to 57,000 tonnes, pressuring the group's 2026 mined-copper target of 1.2 million tonnes
Zijin Gold International's over-allotment option fully exercised, raising ~HK$3.70bn and diluting Zijin Mining's indirect stake in the subsidiary from 86.70% to 85.00%

Zijin Gold terminated its ~US$4bn bid for Allied Gold after conditions could not reasonably be satisfied by the outside date; instead completed a private-placement subscription for a 9.2% stake in Allied Gold
Republic of Congo banned exports of copper and cobalt concentrates, underscoring resource-nationalism risk across Zijin's DRC-adjacent and Central African operating footprint

Interim dividend plan of RMB11.1bn declared (10 July 2026), brought forward from the usual cadence; combined with the RMB10.1bn final 2025 dividend paid end-June 2026, cumulative calendar-year dividends surpassed RMB20bn for the first time

H1 2026 operating highlights: mined gold +13.4% YoY to 46.7 tonnes; mined copper -5.7% YoY to 534,407 tonnes (but +4.8% excluding Kamoa); lithium carbonate equivalent output +496% YoY to 43,596 tonnes as new lithium projects ramp; debt-to-asset ratio fell below 50% for the first time since 2012 (49.55%)
Manono Lithium Mine (DRC) dense media separation plant began production about one month ahead of schedule

Zijin Gold International agreed to take effective control (~25.85% enlarged stake) of Chifeng Jilong Gold Mining for ~RMB18.26bn (~US$2.6bn), adding six gold mines and one polymetallic mine across China, Southeast Asia and West Africa; deal expected to close H2 2026
Zijin Mining's market capitalization passed US$100bn, making it the world's third-largest mining company by market cap (behind BHP and Rio Tinto, ahead of Glencore)

Kamoa-Kakula Copper Mine (DRC) suffered a seismic event and subsequent flooding that suspended operations; Ivanhoe Mines (partner) cut 2026 guidance to 290,000-330,000 tonnes from 380,000-420,000 tonnes as staged dewatering and ramp-up continue

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report / FY2025 Annual Report Executive Summary
guidance.fiscal_year: FY2026 and Three-Year Plan (2026-2028) / Long-range Objective through 2035

items.target: ~1.2 million tonnes (group-wide) for 2026, originally guided at 1.20 million tonnes; 1.50-1.60 million tonnes by 2028
items.notes: 2026 target under pressure from the Kamoa-Kakula flood -- company disclosed its attributable copper output could be cut by 22,000-57,000 tonnes versus plan; FY2024 actual 1.07mt, FY2025 actual 1.09mt (per FY2025 annual report chart)
FY2024 actual 73 tonnes, FY2025 actual 90 tonnes; H1 2026 already running +13.4% YoY at 46.7 tonnes, supportive of the 105-tonne 2026E target

FY2025 actual 25.5 thousand tonnes; H1 2026 actual already 43.6 thousand tonnes (+496% YoY), ahead of pace for the 120kt 2026E figure given new capacity ramp-ups at Lakkor Tso, Tres Quebradas, Xiangyuan and Manono
FY2025 actual 11.5 thousand tonnes; Shapinggou Molybdenum Mine processing project construction began June 2026

items.target: 35% of cumulative distributable profit over 2026-2028 (cash dividends)
items.notes: Increased from 30% under the prior three-year plan; cumulative calendar-year dividend distributions already exceeded RMB20bn in 2026 (final 2025 dividend RMB10.1bn + 2026 interim dividend RMB11.1bn), with the interim payment timing accelerated

items.target: Top-3 globally in mine-produced copper and mine-produced gold volumes by 2028; leading-edge global ranking with certain indicators 1st globally by 2035
items.vs_prior: new (Three-Year Plan 2026-2028 and Long-range Objective through 2035, approved by the 9th Board term in 2026)
items.notes: Explicitly framed as guiding/aspirational targets, not commitments; company retains right to adjust based on circumstances

guidance.management_commentary: Management (new Chairman Zou Laichang, appointed 31 December 2025 following the retirement of founder Chen Jinghe) reiterated the strategic pivot from 'scale leadership' to 'value leadership', with an overarching principle of 'improving quality, increasing production, controlling costs, and boosting profitability.' Management explicitly flagged that 2026 production of 'certain mineral products was relatively behind the scheduled progress of the annual plan' due to the Kamoa-Kakula flood and safety-related suspension of certain domestic mines, while emphasizing 'zero supply disruption' resilience elsewhere in the global supply chain despite Middle East geopolitical escalation. All forward-looking production and financial figures are explicitly disclaimed in filings as non-binding goals, not profit forecasts or commitments.

bull_case: Direct, high-quality leveraged exposure to a structural multi-year gold and copper bull market (AI/electrification-driven copper demand, debasement/de-dollarization-driven gold demand), with H1 2026 net profit already up 68-76% YoY on price alone

Best-in-class growth pipeline across all three strategic metals simultaneously -- copper (Julong, Kamoa-Kakula, Serbia, Zhunuo), gold (Zijin Gold International platform plus pending Chifeng Gold consolidation) and lithium (Lakkor Tso, Tres Quebradas, Manono, Xiangyuan) -- each with multi-year production ramps still ahead, none fully priced into 2025 base-year results

Proven low-cost operator and disciplined, successful M&A track record (Kamoa-Kakula, Julong, Serbia Zijin Copper, Zangge Mining, Chifeng Gold) consistently adding reserves/resources at attractive valuations, funded increasingly by strong internally generated cash flow rather than dilutive equity

Improving balance sheet (debt-to-asset ratio below 50% for the first time since 2012) alongside a rising dividend payout ratio (raised to 35%) and accelerated dividend cadence, improving the capital-return story for a historically capex-heavy miner

Top-3 global mining company status and rapidly climbing Forbes/Fortune rankings reflect increasing scale, liquidity and index inclusion that can support a re-rating versus historically lower multiples assigned to Chinese-domiciled miners
bear_case: Results are highly dependent on a continuation of historically elevated and volatile gold, copper and silver prices (gold swung from ~US$5,500/oz to below US$4,000/oz within H1 2026 alone); a sustained pullback in metal prices would sharply compress the extraordinary profit growth seen in FY2025/H1 2026

Operational and geopolitical risk concentrated in the DRC, Serbia and other emerging/frontier jurisdictions -- the Kamoa-Kakula flood alone could cut 2026 attributable copper output by up to 57,000 tonnes, and resource-nationalism (e.g., Congo's copper/cobalt export ban) is explicitly rising as a sector-wide risk per management's own commentary

Complex, rapidly evolving corporate structure (multiple listed subsidiaries -- Zijin Gold International, Zangge Mining, soon-to-be-consolidated Chifeng Gold -- plus large recurring M&A) raises governance, minority-interest and capital-allocation discipline concerns
CNY-denominated financials against an HKD-denominated H-share quote complicate cross-currency valuation and create potential mispricing risk for investors who do not explicitly bridge the fx rate

Chinese state-shareholder linkage (Minxi Xinghang, a Fujian county government vehicle) and broad emerging-market/geopolitical exposure could weigh on the multiple some Western investors are willing to pay versus comparably sized Western-domiciled diversified miners (BHP, Rio Tinto, Glencore)

Heavy ongoing capex across many simultaneous large projects (Julong phase 3, Zhunuo, Manono, Shapinggou, Serbia expansion) could pressure free cash flow and returns if commodity prices soften even moderately from current highs
